subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The very large surface area of the small intestine for absorption is produced by:
options: A dense capillary network in the submucosa only
Villi and microvilli on the epithelial cells
questions.explain: Folded villi each covered in microvilli (the brush border) massively increase the absorptive surface area of the ileum.

questions.q: On a hot, sunny day a plant's rate of photosynthesis levels off and does not rise with further light. Which factor is most likely limiting?
questions.explain: When light is already plentiful, CO2 concentration commonly becomes the limiting factor that caps the rate.

questions.q: Why can small non-polar molecules such as oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the membrane by simple diffusion?
options: They are repelled by the hydrophobic core
They are small and non-polar, so they dissolve in and pass through the hydrophobic phospholipid bilayer
questions.explain: Being small and non-polar, these molecules dissolve in the lipid bilayer and diffuse directly across down their gradient.

questions.q: Why is the Calvin cycle described as light-independent even though it stops in the dark?
options: It directly absorbs light to fix carbon
Its enzymes are destroyed by light
It does not itself use light, but depends on ATP and reduced NADP from the light reactions
questions.explain: The reactions need no light directly, but they soon halt without the ATP and reduced NADP supplied in the light.

questions.q: Active transport differs from facilitated diffusion because active transport:
options: moves substances down a concentration gradient
requires ATP to move substances against their concentration gradient via carrier proteins
questions.explain: Active transport uses energy from ATP hydrolysis to pump substances against their gradient through carrier proteins.

questions.q: Which factor would increase the permeability of a cell membrane?
options: An increase in temperature, increasing phospholipid movement and creating gaps
A decrease in temperature, increasing phospholipid order
questions.explain: Higher temperatures increase phospholipid kinetic energy and fluidity, and can denature membrane proteins, increasing permeability.

questions.q: Fetal haemoglobin has a dissociation curve to the LEFT of adult haemoglobin because:
options: It must release oxygen more readily to the placenta
It has a higher affinity for oxygen, allowing it to load oxygen from maternal blood at the placenta
It is less saturated at every partial pressure of oxygen
questions.explain: A higher oxygen affinity (curve to the left) lets fetal Hb take up oxygen from maternal Hb across the placenta.

questions.q: Cholesterol in the cell membrane functions to:
options: regulate membrane fluidity and stability by sitting between phospholipids
questions.explain: Cholesterol fits between phospholipid tails, restricting their movement to maintain fluidity and mechanical stability across temperatures.

questions.q: Out of every six molecules of triose phosphate (TP) made in the Calvin cycle, how many are used to regenerate RuBP?
questions.explain: Five of every six TP molecules are recycled to regenerate RuBP, leaving one to contribute to carbohydrate.

questions.q: What are the products of the photolysis of water during the light-dependent stage?
questions.explain: Splitting water yields electrons for photosystem II, protons for the gradient, and oxygen as a by-product.

questions.q: A red blood cell placed in pure water bursts (haemolysis) because:
options: water leaves the cell by osmosis
water enters down a water potential gradient and the cell has no rigid wall to resist swelling
solutes enter the cell by active transport
the membrane actively pumps water in
questions.explain: Pure water has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm, so water enters by osmosis; lacking a cell wall, the animal cell swells and lyses.

questions.q: Two cells are in contact: cell A has a water potential of -400 kPa and cell B has -750 kPa. Water will move:
options: from cell B to cell A
not at all because the cells are isolated
in both directions equally with no net movement
from cell A to cell B
questions.explain: Water moves from a higher (less negative) water potential to a lower (more negative) one, i.e. from A (-400) to B (-750).
